Techkeyy opened issue #107: Query errors are replaced with "internal query execution error" on both transports, so clients cannot diagnose failures
Building a graph application on HydraDB, every failing write returned the same opaque string on the client:

```
internal query execution error
```

The real cause is logged server-side as `Bolt suppressed internal graph error`, but the client never receives it. Both transports do this:

- `src/client/bolt/values.rs:271`
- `src/client/http.rs:433`

Any unmatched `GraphError` is mapped to that generic string.

### Why this is costly

I lost several hours to this. Every write in my ingest was failing while reads succeeded. With no error detail, the only hypotheses available were about my Cypher, so I rewrote working queries repeatedly. The actual cause was unrelated to the query (filesystem permissions, filed separately).

The failure mode is that the message points at the wrong layer. A storage permission error reads as a syntax problem, and there is nothing in the client response to suggest otherwise.

### What helped, once I found it

```bash
docker logs $(docker ps --filter name=hydradb --format '{{.Names}}' | head -1) --tail 60
```

aetosdios27 commented: started poking at this one. good write-up, easy to act on.

turns out there's already a `GraphError::class()` method (`src/core/error.rs`) that returns a coarse category — "storage", "query", "contention", "timeout", etc, 12 of them total. it's built for exactly this: safe to hand to a client, doesn't leak the actual detail. right now it's only wired into telemetry, not into either client-facing error path.

so the fix is small: in the catch-all arms of `graph_error_to_bolt` (`src/client/bolt/values.rs`) and `HttpApiError::from_graph_ref` (`src/client/http.rs`), swap the hardcoded `"internal query execution error"` string for one that includes `error.class()`. no wire framing changes, no new types, just the fallback message.

working on a PR for this now. wanted to comment first in case there's a reason this wasn't already done, or a preferred error format (thinking `internal query execution error (storage)`, happy to change the shape).
